title: Shy, supping with the godless, he sneaks the cup. A sire in Ultonian Antrim bade it him. Visits him here on quarter days. Mr Magee, sir, there’s a gentleman to see you. Me? Says he’s your father, sir. Give me my Wordsworth. Enter Magee Mor Matthew, a rugged rough rugheaded kern, in strossers with a buttoned codpiece, his nether stocks bemired with clauber of ten forests, a wand of wilding in his hand.
html_source: Stephen’s imagining. As noted previously, Magee is the birth-name of Eglinton. By adopting a pseudonym, he could be said to have denied his father, thus again echoing the alienation theme.
